q.en: You reach an intersection where the sign facing you has eight sides and is red with white letters. What must you do?
q.zh: 你来到一个路口，面对你的标志有八条边，红底白字。你必须怎么做？

en: Come to a complete stop, then proceed when it is safe
Stop only if other vehicles are coming
Treat it like a yield sign and keep rolling slowly
Slow down and go if the road looks clear
zh: 完全停稳，确认安全后再通过
只有其他车辆驶来时才停车
当作让行标志，慢慢滑行通过
减速，如果路面看起来没车就通过

explanation.en: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. Stop completely at the stop line, or before the crosswalk or intersection if there is no stop line, yield to vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection, and go only when it is safe. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 八边形标志是停车标志。应在停车线处完全停稳；没有停车线时，在人行横道或路口之前停稳，让行路口内的车辆和行人，确认安全后才能通过。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A sign shaped like an upside-down triangle is posted at the entrance to a busy road. What does this shape always mean?
q.zh: 一条繁忙道路的入口处立着一个倒三角形标志。这个形状始终表示什么？

en: A railroad crossing is ahead
No passing is allowed
Yield — slow down and give the right-of-way if needed
Stop for exactly three seconds
zh: 让行——减速，必要时让出路权

explanation.en: The inverted triangle is the yield sign, the only sign with this shape. Slow down, look both ways, and yield to pedestrians, bicycles, and vehicles before proceeding when safe. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 倒三角形是让行标志，也是唯一这种形状的标志。应减速、左右观察，让行行人、自行车和车辆，安全时再通过。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: Warning signs that alert you to hazards ahead are usually which color and shape?
q.zh: 提醒你前方有危险的警告标志通常是什么颜色和形状？

en: Green diamonds
Orange circles
Yellow diamonds
Red rectangles

explanation.en: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs, and yellow is the general warning color. They tell you about special conditions or hazards ahead so you can slow down and get ready. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 菱形标志是警告标志，黄色是通用警告色。这类标志提示前方有特殊路况或危险，以便你减速并做好准备。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: You see an orange sign with black lettering as you approach a stretch of road work. What is orange used for on Maryland roads?
q.zh: 你接近一段道路施工区时，看到一块橙底黑字的标志。在马里兰州道路上，橙色表示什么？

en: Services such as food and gas
A recreation area
A school zone
Construction and maintenance work areas

explanation.en: Orange is the color for construction and maintenance work-area warnings. Slow down, watch for workers and changed traffic patterns, and obey work-zone signs. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 橙色是施工与养护作业区的警告色。应减速、注意工人和变化的交通组织，并遵守施工区标志。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A five-sided (pentagon-shaped) sign appears on a residential street. What is it warning you about?
q.zh: 一条住宅区街道上出现了一个五边形标志。它在提醒你注意什么？

en: A school zone or school crossing
A rest area is near
A divided highway begins
A hospital entrance
zh: 学校区域或学校过街处

explanation.en: The pentagon shape warns of school zones and marks school crossings. Slow down and watch carefully for children. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 五边形标志提示学校区域并标示学校过街处。应减速并仔细观察儿童。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: On a rural road, a round yellow sign is posted well before the tracks. What does a round sign mean?
q.zh: 在一条乡村道路上，铁轨前方较远处立着一个圆形黄色标志。圆形标志表示什么？

en: A traffic circle is ahead
A railroad crossing is ahead
The exact spot where tracks cross the road
Trains are prohibited here
zh: 铁轨与道路交叉的确切位置

explanation.en: A round sign is the advance warning for a railroad crossing ahead. The crossing itself is identified by the crossbuck where the tracks cross the road. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 圆形标志是铁路道口的前方预告。道口本身的位置由道口处的叉架标志（crossbuck）标示。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: Which sign identifies the exact location where railroad tracks cross the road at grade?
q.zh: 哪个标志标示铁轨与道路平面交叉的确切位置？

en: A round yellow sign
An X-shaped crossbuck
A diamond with a train symbol
A pennant-shaped sign
zh: 带火车图案的菱形标志

explanation.en: The crossbuck — the X-shaped sign — identifies the location of a highway-rail grade crossing. The round sign only warns that a crossing is ahead. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 叉架标志（X形）标示公路与铁路平面道口的位置。圆形标志只是预告前方有道口。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A pennant-shaped sign is posted on the left side of a two-lane road. What is it telling you?
q.zh: 一条双车道道路左侧立着一个三角旗形标志。它在告诉你什么？

en: Left turns are banned ahead
A no-passing zone begins here
A side road enters from the left
The left lane ends
zh: 此处开始是禁止超车区

explanation.en: The pennant shape marks the start of a no-passing zone. Do not pass other vehicles there. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 三角旗形标志标示禁止超车区的起点。在该区域不得超越其他车辆。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: At the exit ramp of a highway, a red-and-white sign reads DO NOT ENTER. You are about to drive up that ramp. What should you do?
q.zh: 在高速公路出口匝道处，一块红白标志写着“禁止驶入”。你正要驶上那条匝道。你应该怎么做？

en: Honk and enter quickly
Enter only if no cars are coming down
Do not enter — you would be driving against traffic
Enter slowly with hazard lights on
zh: 只有没有车下来时才能驶入
打开危险报警灯慢慢驶入

explanation.en: Do Not Enter signs mark roadways where traffic moves in the opposite direction. Entering would put you head-on against traffic. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: “禁止驶入”标志标示交通方向相反的道路。驶入将与来车正面相对。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: You turned onto a street and immediately see a WRONG WAY sign facing you. What is the safest response?
q.zh: 你拐进一条街道后，立刻看到一块面对你的“错误方向”标志。最安全的做法是什么？

en: Turn around or pull over safely as soon as possible — you are going against traffic
Ignore it if the street is empty
Speed up to reach the next intersection
Keep driving in the left lane
zh: 尽快安全掉头或靠边停车——你正在逆行
如果街上没车就不用管

explanation.en: A Wrong Way sign means you are traveling against the flow of traffic. Get out of the opposing flow safely as soon as you can. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: “错误方向”标志表示你正逆着交通流行驶。应尽快安全地脱离对向车流。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A black-and-white sign shows an arrow pointing right with the words ONE WAY. What does it require?
q.zh: 一块黑白标志上有一个向右的箭头和“单行道”字样。它要求什么？

en: Right turns are allowed on red here
Traffic on this road may travel only in the direction of the arrow
Parking is allowed on the right side only
You must turn right at the next corner
zh: 此路交通只能按箭头方向行驶
你必须在下一个路口右转

explanation.en: A One Way sign means traffic can only go in the direction of the arrow. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: “单行道”标志表示交通只能按箭头所指方向行驶。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A rectangular black-on-white sign shows a number for speed. What does that number represent?
q.zh: 一块长方形黑字白底标志上标着一个速度数字。这个数字表示什么？

en: The average speed of traffic
The suggested speed in bad weather
The slowest speed you may drive
The maximum legal speed for that part of the road under ideal conditions
zh: 恶劣天气下的建议速度
理想条件下该路段的最高法定速度

explanation.en: The speed limit sign states the maximum speed limit for that part of the road. The posted limit is the maximum under ideal conditions, and you must still slow down when conditions require it. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 限速标志标明该路段的最高限速。该限速是理想条件下的最大值，路况需要时仍必须减速。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A sign shows a left-turn arrow with a red circle and slash over it. What is prohibited?
q.zh: 一个标志上左转箭头被红圈斜杠覆盖。禁止什么？

en: Parking on the left
Driving in the left lane
Turning left
Passing on the left

explanation.en: A red circle with a slash over a left-turn arrow means no left turn is allowed at that location. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 左转箭头上带红圈斜杠表示该处禁止左转。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A sign shows a U-shaped arrow crossed out by a red circle and slash. What maneuver is banned?
q.zh: 一个标志上U形箭头被红圈斜杠划掉。禁止哪种操作？

en: Turning right on red
Making a U-turn
Backing up
Merging

explanation.en: The crossed-out U-shaped arrow means U-turns are prohibited there. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 被划掉的U形箭头表示此处禁止掉头。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: You are looking for a place to leave your car and see a NO PARKING sign on the post. What does it mean for you?
q.zh: 你想找地方停车，看到杆子上有一块“禁止停车”标志。这对你意味着什么？

en: You may park if you stay in the car
You may not park there
You may park only at night
You may park for up to 10 minutes
zh: 只要人留在车里就可以停

explanation.en: A No Parking regulatory sign prohibits parking in that area. You must find a place that is clearly meant for parking. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: “禁止停车”管制标志禁止在该区域停车。应寻找明确用于停车的地点。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A yellow diamond sign shows a person walking inside a crosswalk symbol. Drivers should expect:
q.zh: 一块黄色菱形标志上画着人行横道中的行人。驾驶员应预料到：

en: A sidewalk ends ahead
A bus stop ahead
A hiking trail parking lot
Pedestrians crossing the road ahead

explanation.en: That warning sign marks a pedestrian crossing ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop for people crossing. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 该警告标志标示前方有行人过街处。应减速并准备为过街行人停车。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A yellow diamond shows the road bending to the right ahead. What should you do before the bend?
q.zh: 一块黄色菱形标志显示前方道路向右弯曲。进入弯道前你应该怎么做？

en: Turn on your high beams only
Slow down and be ready for the curve
Shift to the left side of the road
Speed up to get through quickly
zh: 减速并为弯道做好准备

explanation.en: A curve warning sign tells you the road bends ahead. Reduce speed before the curve, especially since sharp curves and hills limit how far you can see. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 弯道警告标志提示前方道路转弯。应在弯道前减速，特别是急弯和坡道会限制视距。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A warning sign shows an arrow making a sharp, hairpin-style turn. Compared with an ordinary curve sign, this warns of:
q.zh: 一个警告标志上的箭头呈急剧的发夹式转弯。与普通弯道标志相比，它警告的是：

en: A turn that only trucks must slow for
A much sharper turn that needs a greater speed reduction
A turn you may take at full speed
A one-way turn lane
zh: 只有卡车需要减速的转弯
急得多的转弯，需要更大减速

explanation.en: The sharp-turn warning sign indicates a turn much sharper than a regular curve. Slow down more and proceed with care. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 急转弯警告标志表示转弯比普通弯道急得多。应更多减速并小心通过。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A yellow diamond shows a car with wavy skid lines behind it. When is this hazard most likely?
q.zh: 一块黄色菱形标志上画着一辆车，后面有波浪形打滑线。这种危险最可能在何时出现？

en: Only on gravel roads
When traffic is stopped
On dry summer afternoons
When the road is wet

explanation.en: That is the Slippery When Wet warning. Wet roads reduce traction, so slow down and avoid sudden braking or steering. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 这是“路面湿滑”警告标志。湿路会降低抓地力，应减速并避免急刹车或急打方向。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A warning sign shows two lanes coming together into one stream of traffic. What should you prepare for?
q.zh: 一个警告标志显示两条车道汇成一股车流。你应做好什么准备？

en: A lane reserved for buses
A divided highway ending
Traffic merging ahead — adjust speed and position to merge safely
A toll plaza
zh: 前方有车辆汇入——调整速度和位置以安全汇流

explanation.en: The merge warning tells you traffic will be joining or lanes will combine ahead. Be ready to adjust speed and leave space so merging can happen safely. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 汇流警告标志提示前方有车辆汇入或车道合并。应准备调整速度并留出空间，使汇流安全完成。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A warning sign shows two arrows pointing in opposite directions, one up and one down. It warns that:
q.zh: 一个警告标志上有两个方向相反的箭头，一个向上一个向下。它警告：

en: You are leaving a one-way street and entering two-way traffic
Two highways run parallel
Bicycles travel both directions
The road becomes one-way
zh: 你正离开单行道，进入双向交通

explanation.en: The two-way traffic warning tells you the roadway ahead carries traffic in both directions, so expect oncoming vehicles in the other lane. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 双向交通警告标志提示前方道路双向通行，应预料对向车道有来车。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A warning sign shows two roadways separated by a median strip. It is telling you that:
q.zh: 一个警告标志显示两条被中央分隔带分开的道路。它在告诉你：

en: You must use the median to turn
The divided highway is ending
Trucks must use the right roadway
A divided highway begins ahead
zh: 前方开始是分隔式公路

explanation.en: That sign warns that a divided road begins ahead — traffic directions will be separated by a median or barrier. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 该标志警告前方开始是分隔式道路——两个方向的交通将被分隔带或屏障分开。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A yellow diamond shows a traffic light symbol. What should you be ready to do?
q.zh: 一块黄色菱形标志上画着交通信号灯图案。你应准备做什么？

en: Turn around
Speed up before the light changes
Expect a railroad signal instead
Stop for a traffic signal ahead if required
zh: 前方有交通信号灯，必要时停车

explanation.en: The signal-ahead warning tells you a traffic signal is coming up, possibly where you cannot yet see it. Be ready to stop. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 信号灯前方警告提示前方有交通信号灯，可能你还看不到。应做好停车准备。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: You see a yellow diamond with an octagon symbol and an upward arrow. What lies ahead?
q.zh: 你看到一块黄色菱形标志，上面有八边形图案和向上的箭头。前方有什么？

en: A stop sign ahead
A parking area
A road closed sign
A detour around a stop line

explanation.en: That is the Stop Ahead warning. A stop sign is coming up, so prepare to make a complete stop. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 这是“前方停车标志”警告。前方有停车标志，应准备完全停车。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A yellow diamond shows a leaping deer. Where should you be especially alert?
q.zh: 一块黄色菱形标志上画着一只跳跃的鹿。你应在哪种路段特别警觉？

en: In parking garages
In areas where deer or other wildlife may cross the road
Near airports only
Near schools
zh: 鹿或其他野生动物可能穿越道路的区域

explanation.en: The deer/wildlife crossing warning marks areas where animals may enter the road. Slow down and scan the roadside, especially in low light. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 鹿/野生动物穿越警告标示动物可能进入道路的区域。应减速并扫视路边，光线较暗时尤其注意。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A diamond sign shows a worker with a flag. What should you expect ahead?
q.zh: 一个菱形标志上画着一名手持旗帜的工人。前方应预料到什么？

en: A parade route
A school crossing guard
A flagger directing traffic in a work zone
A pedestrian with the right-of-way
zh: 施工区里指挥交通的旗手

explanation.en: The flagger-ahead warning means a person with a flag is directing traffic through a work zone. Slow down and obey the flagger's directions. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: “前方有旗手”警告表示有人持旗在施工区指挥交通。应减速并服从旗手的指挥。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A warning sign shows a bicycle and a pedestrian together. It most likely marks:
q.zh: 一个警告标志上同时画着自行车和行人。它最可能标示：

en: A place where pedestrians and bicyclists cross the road
A no-bicycle zone
A bicycle repair shop
A bike lane that ends
zh: 行人与骑行者过街的地点

explanation.en: The pedestrian and bicycle crossing warning marks where people walking and biking cross the road. Slow down and yield as required. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 行人与自行车过街警告标示步行和骑行者过街的地点。应减速并按规定让行。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A warning sign shows one lane narrowing and disappearing into another. What is about to happen?
q.zh: 一个警告标志显示一条车道变窄并汇入另一条车道。即将发生什么？

en: The road widens
A lane ends ahead — merge safely into the remaining lane
A new lane is added
An exit-only lane begins
zh: 前方车道结束——安全汇入剩余车道

explanation.en: The lane-ends warning tells you a lane is ending ahead. Check traffic, signal if changing lanes, and merge when it is safe. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 车道结束警告提示前方车道结束。应观察交通、变道时打灯，在安全时汇入。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A warning sign shows arrows moving in a circle. As you approach what it warns of, you must:
q.zh: 一个警告标志显示箭头沿圆圈运动。接近它所警告的地点时，你必须：

en: Yield to traffic already traveling in the circle
Speed up to enter before others
Use the leftmost lane at all times
Stop completely for one full minute
zh: 让行已在环岛内行驶的车辆
加速抢在他人之前进入

explanation.en: The sign warns of a traffic circle (roundabout) ahead. At the circle you must always yield to traffic already in it. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings; Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 该标志警告前方有环岛。在环岛处必须始终让行已在岛内行驶的车辆。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线；第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: Two cars arrive at a four-way stop at exactly the same moment. Which driver goes first?
q.zh: 两辆车同时到达四向停车路口。哪位驾驶员先行？

en: The driver on the left
The larger vehicle
The driver on the right
Whoever honks first

explanation.en: When two drivers arrive at an intersection at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way; the other driver yields. See Section 3: Basic Driving.
explanation.zh: 两名驾驶员同时到达路口时，右侧驾驶员拥有路权，另一方应让行。见第3节：基本驾驶。

q.en: You are turning left at an intersection while traffic approaches from the opposite direction. Who has the right-of-way?
q.zh: 你在路口左转时，对面有车辆驶来。谁拥有路权？

en: You do, because you signaled first
You split the intersection equally
The opposing traffic — you must yield to it
Whoever is driving faster

explanation.en: A driver turning left must yield to drivers in the opposing traffic lane. See Section 3: Basic Driving.
explanation.zh: 左转驾驶员必须让行对向车道的车辆。见第3节：基本驾驶。

q.en: You pull out of a private driveway onto a public street. What does right-of-way require of you?
q.zh: 你从私人车道驶出到公共街道上。路权规则要求你怎么做？

en: Enter quickly before traffic arrives
Yield to drivers already on the road you are entering
Enter without stopping if your driveway is steep
Traffic on the street must yield to you
zh: 在车流到达前快速驶入
让行你所进入道路上的车辆
如果车道很陡可以不停直接驶入

explanation.en: Drivers entering a road from a driveway or private road must yield to drivers already on that road. See Section 3: Basic Driving.
explanation.zh: 从车道或私人道路进入道路的驾驶员必须让行已在该道路上行驶的车辆。见第3节：基本驾驶。

q.en: You are on an entrance ramp merging toward a highway. The vehicles already on the highway are moving steadily. Who yields?
q.zh: 你在入口匝道上正要汇入高速公路，高速公路上的车辆正稳定行驶。谁让行？

en: The slowest highway driver yields
You must yield to drivers already on the highway
Nobody yields; merge at any speed
Highway drivers must yield to you
zh: 高速公路上最慢的驾驶员让行
你必须让行已在高速公路上的车辆
谁都不让；以任何速度汇入
高速公路驾驶员必须让你

explanation.en: Drivers on an entrance or acceleration ramp yield to drivers already on the highway. Use the acceleration lane to match traffic speed, then merge. See Section 3: Basic Driving; Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 在入口或加速车道上的驾驶员应让行已在高速公路上的车辆。应利用加速车道匹配车流速度后再汇入。见第3节：基本驾驶；第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: Your light turns green, but a pedestrian and another car are still inside the intersection. What should you do?
q.zh: 你的信号灯变绿了，但一名行人和一辆车还在路口内。你应该怎么做？

en: Yield to the pedestrian and the vehicle already in the intersection
Proceed — green means go regardless
Drive around them on the shoulder
Honk until they move
zh: 让行行人和已在路口内的车辆
通过——绿灯就是无条件通行

explanation.en: Even on a green signal, or a green arrow, you must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 即使是绿灯或绿色箭头，也必须让行已在路口内的行人和车辆。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: The traffic light ahead turns yellow while you are still far enough away to stop safely. What does a steady yellow signal mean?
q.zh: 前方信号灯变黄时，你的距离还足够安全停车。持续黄灯表示什么？

en: The signal is changing from green to red — stop safely if you can
Stop only if a camera is present
Speed up before it turns red
Yellow gives you the right-of-way over everyone
zh: 信号正由绿变红——能安全停就停
黄灯时你拥有对所有人的路权

explanation.en: A steady yellow means the signal is about to change to red. If you can stop safely, do so; if you are too close to stop safely, proceed carefully through. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 持续黄灯表示信号即将变红。能安全停车就应停车；如果距离太近无法安全停车，则小心通过。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: You stop at a red light where no sign prohibits turning. After a complete stop, which turns may you make?
q.zh: 你在红灯前停车，该处没有禁止转弯的标志。完全停稳后，你可以做哪些转弯？

en: Left turns from any two-way street
Turn right, or turn left from a one-way street onto another one-way street — yielding to pedestrians and all other traffic
Any turn, including a U-turn
Right turns only, without stopping again
zh: 右转，或从单行道向另一条单行道左转——并让行行人和所有其他交通

explanation.en: After a complete stop at a red signal, and unless a sign prohibits it, you may turn right or turn left from one one-way street to another, yielding to pedestrians and all other traffic. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 在红灯前完全停稳后，除非标志禁止，你可以右转，或从一条单行道向另一条单行道左转，并须让行行人和所有其他交通。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: Approaching an intersection, the signal is completely dark and not working. How must you treat it?
q.zh: 接近路口时，信号灯完全熄灭、不工作。你必须如何处理？

en: Stop at the stop line, or before the crosswalk or intersection, and yield to vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection
Drive through at normal speed
Stop only during rush hour
Treat it as a green light for your direction
zh: 在停车线，或人行横道、路口之前停车，并让行路口内的车辆和行人

explanation.en: When a traffic signal is not working, stop at the stop line — or before the crosswalk or intersection if there is none — yield to vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection, and proceed only when safe. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 信号灯不工作时，应在停车线处停车；没有停车线时在人行横道或路口前停车，让行路口内的车辆和行人，安全时再通过。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: The signal facing you is flashing red. What must you do before proceeding?
q.zh: 面对你的信号灯在闪烁红光。通过前你必须怎么做？

en: Slow down and continue with caution
Come to a complete stop, yield to all other traffic and pedestrians, and go when the way is clear
Treat it exactly like a yellow light
Stop only if cross traffic is present
zh: 完全停车，让行所有其他交通和行人，路通畅后再通过

explanation.en: A flashing red signal requires a complete stop, then yield to all traffic and pedestrians and proceed when clear — like a stop sign. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 闪烁红灯要求完全停车，然后让行所有交通和行人，通畅后再通过——如同停车标志。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: The signal facing you is flashing yellow. What must you do?
q.zh: 面对你的信号灯在闪烁黄光。你必须怎么做？

en: Speed up to clear the intersection
Stop and wait for green
Slow down and proceed with caution
Come to a complete stop

explanation.en: A flashing yellow signal means slow down and proceed with caution; it does not require a complete stop. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 闪烁黄灯表示减速并小心通过，不需要完全停车。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: Overhead lane signals show a red X above the lane you are in. What does that mean?
q.zh: 你所在车道上方信号显示红色X。这表示什么？

en: You must never drive in a lane under a red X
You may use the lane for left turns only
The lane closes in one hour
Trucks only may use the lane
zh: 绝不能在红色X下方的车道行驶
车道将在一小时后关闭
只有卡车可使用该车道

explanation.en: Lane-use signals control reversible lanes. You must never drive in a lane under a red X signal. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 车道使用信号控制可变车道。绝不能在红色X信号下方的车道行驶。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: An overhead lane signal changes to a steady yellow X above your lane. What should you do?
q.zh: 你车道上方的信号变为持续黄色X。你应该怎么做？

en: Use the lane only for passing
Stop immediately in the lane
Ignore it until it turns red
Move out of the lane as soon as you safely can
zh: 在能安全做到时尽快驶离该车道

explanation.en: A steady yellow X means you should move out of that lane as soon as you safely can. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 持续黄色X表示应尽快安全地驶离该车道。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: On a two-lane road, the center line on your side is a solid yellow line. What does that line mean for passing?
q.zh: 在双车道道路上，你一侧的中央线是黄色实线。这条线对超车意味着什么？

en: Passing is allowed at night only
You may pass bicycles only
Passing is allowed with extra care
You may not pass — the solid yellow line is on your side
zh: 不得超车——黄色实线在你一侧

explanation.en: You may not pass where the solid yellow line is on your side of the road, or where there are double solid yellow lines. See Section 3: Basic Driving; Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 当黄色实线在你一侧时不得超车，双黄实线时也不得超车。见第3节：基本驾驶；第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

q.en: You need to turn left into a driveway across double solid yellow lines. Is that allowed?
q.zh: 你需要越过双黄实线左转进入一条车道。这样做允许吗？

en: No — double yellow lines may never be crossed
Only if a police officer waves you through
Yes — you may make a left turn across double solid yellow lines, though passing is not allowed
Only on weekends
zh: 不允许——双黄线永不能越过
只有警察挥手放行时才行
允许——可以越过双黄实线左转，但不得超车

explanation.en: Double solid yellow lines ban passing in either direction, but a left turn across them is allowed, for example into a driveway. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 双黄实线禁止双向超车，但允许越过它左转，例如进入车道。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: A center line is made of one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. Traffic on the broken-line side may:
q.zh: 中央线由一条黄色实线和一条黄色虚线组成。虚线一侧的车辆可以：

en: Pass only when following a truck
Pass carefully — passing is permitted from the broken-line side only
Cross into oncoming lanes freely
Never pass
zh: 小心超车——只允许虚线一侧超车

explanation.en: With solid-plus-broken yellow lines, careful passing is allowed for traffic on the broken-line side and not allowed for traffic on the solid-line side. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 黄实线加黄虚线时，虚线一侧可小心超车，实线一侧不得超车。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: White crosswalk lines are painted across the road at an intersection. What do they show?
q.zh: 路口处路面画有白色人行横道线。它们标示什么？

en: Where bicycles must dismount
Where vehicles must stop for fuel checks
A loading zone
Where pedestrians cross
zh: 车辆必须停车接受燃油检查处

explanation.en: Crosswalk lines are white, solid lines that show where pedestrians cross. Most intersections have a crosswalk even if it is not marked. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 人行横道线是白色实线，标示行人过街的位置。大多数路口即使没有标线也有人行横道。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: You are about to pass a car traveling in the same direction. When may you return to your original lane?
q.zh: 你正要超越同向行驶的一辆车。何时可以返回原车道？

en: As soon as your front bumper passes theirs
Only after you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rear-view mirror
After honking twice
After traveling one full mile
zh: 你的前保险杠一超过对方就可以
只有在后视镜中能看到被超车辆的两个大灯后

explanation.en: Before returning to your lane, you must be able to see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rear-view mirror. See Section 3: Basic Driving.
explanation.zh: 返回原车道前，必须在后视镜中能看到被超车辆的两个大灯。见第3节：基本驾驶。

q.en: Which of these is a situation where passing on the right is allowed in Maryland?
q.zh: 以下哪种情况在马里兰州允许从右侧超车？

en: When the vehicle ahead is about to make a left turn and you can pass safely while staying on the road
Within 100 feet of an intersection
On the shoulder of any road
Whenever your lane is moving slowly
zh: 当前车正要左转，且你能在路面上安全超越时
只要你的车道行驶缓慢

explanation.en: Passing on the right is allowed only if it is safe, you stay on the road, and the other vehicle is about to turn left — or you are on an unobstructed multi-lane or one-way road with two or more lanes. Passing on the shoulder is prohibited. See Section 3: Basic Driving.
explanation.zh: 只有在安全、保持在路面上，且对方车辆正要左转时才允许右侧超车——或在无阻碍的多车道或双车道以上单行道上。在路肩上超车是禁止的。见第3节：基本驾驶。

q.en: Another driver begins passing you. What must you do?
q.zh: 另一位驾驶员开始超越你。你必须怎么做？

en: Flash your lights repeatedly
Move to the left
Yield to the passing vehicle and not increase your speed
Speed up so they cannot get in
zh: 让行超车车辆且不加速

explanation.en: When being passed, you must yield to the other vehicle and not increase your speed. See Section 3: Basic Driving.
explanation.zh: 被超车时，必须让行对方车辆且不得加速。见第3节：基本驾驶。

q.en: How close to an intersection or railroad grade crossing does the ban on passing apply when your view is obstructed?
q.zh: 当视线受阻时，禁止超车的规定在距路口或铁路道口多远范围内适用？

en: Within 500 feet
Within 25 feet
Within 100 feet
Within 50 feet

explanation.en: You may not pass when crossing or within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad grade crossing, or within 100 feet of a bridge, elevated road, or tunnel when your view is obstructed. See Section 3: Basic Driving.
explanation.zh: 在路口或铁路道口处或其100英尺以内不得超车；视线受阻时，在桥梁、高架路或隧道的100英尺以内也不得超车。见第3节：基本驾驶。

q.en: Before making a turn, what is the correct sequence according to the manual?
q.zh: 根据手册，转弯前的正确步骤顺序是什么？

en: Signal only after starting the turn
Turn first, then check mirrors
Speed up, then signal at the last second
Check signs and signals, plan the turn, switch on your turn signal, check front, behind, and both sides, and adjust your speed
zh: 先加速，最后时刻再打灯
查看标志和信号、提前规划转弯、打开转向灯、查看前方、后方和两侧，并调整速度

explanation.en: When turning: look for signs and signals, plan before the turning point, signal before the turn, check front, behind, and both sides, and adjust your speed for the turn. See Section 3: Basic Driving.
explanation.zh: 转弯时应：查看标志和信号、在到达转弯点前规划、提前打开转向灯、查看前方、后方和两侧，并调整转弯速度。见第3节：基本驾驶。

q.en: You need to make a U-turn where U-turns are allowed. What must you do first?
q.zh: 你需要在允许掉头的地方掉头。首先必须怎么做？

en: Turn without stopping if the road looks empty
Signal left, stop, and yield to oncoming traffic; when clear, turn into the outside (right-hand) lane going the opposite way
Turn into the left-hand lane of the opposite direction
Honk and turn quickly
zh: 路面看似没车时不用停直接转
打左转向灯、停车并让行对向车辆；通畅后转入对向的外侧（右侧）车道

explanation.en: For a U-turn: check that U-turns are allowed, signal left, stop and yield to oncoming traffic, and when clear turn into the outside or right-hand lane traveling the opposite direction. See Section 3: Basic Driving.
explanation.zh: 掉头时应：先确认允许掉头，打左转向灯，停车让行对向车辆，通畅后转入对向的外侧即右侧车道。见第3节：基本驾驶。

q.en: Generally, where should you position your vehicle on the road?
q.zh: 一般情况下，你应把车辆保持在道路的什么位置？

en: In the left lane at all times
As close to the center as possible
To the right of the center of the road, unless passing, a sign or signal allows otherwise, or an obstruction requires it
Straddling the center line
zh: 在道路中央的右侧，除非超车、标志或信号允许，或障碍物要求改变位置

explanation.en: Keep your vehicle to the right of the center of the road unless you are passing a same-direction vehicle, a sign or signal says it is okay, or something in the way makes a change necessary. See Section 3: Basic Driving.
explanation.zh: 应将车辆保持在道路中央右侧，除非正在超越同向车辆、标志或信号允许，或前方障碍要求改变位置。见第3节：基本驾驶。

q.en: Which statement about lane changes inside an intersection is correct?
q.zh: 关于在路口内变道，下列说法哪项正确？

en: Lane changes in intersections are encouraged
You may drift across lines if you signal
You should not make lane changes when in an intersection, and you should not drift across lane lines
Lane lines do not apply inside intersections
zh: 只要打灯就可以漂移越线
不应在路口内变道，也不应漂移越过车道线

explanation.en: Drive in a single lane, do not drift across lane lines, and do not make lane changes when in an intersection. See Section 3: Basic Driving.
explanation.zh: 应在单一车道内行驶，不要漂移越过车道线，也不要在路口内变道。见第3节：基本驾驶。

q.en: You park along a road with a curb. Which parking steps does the manual require?
q.zh: 你在有路缘的路边停车。手册要求哪些停车步骤？

en: Park as close to the curb as possible, set the parking brake, place the vehicle in gear or Park, check traffic before opening the door, and take your keys and lock up
Never set the parking brake on a flat road
Park as far into traffic as possible and leave the engine running
Leave the keys in the ignition for emergencies
zh: 尽量靠近路缘停车，拉手刹，挂挡或挂P挡，开门前观察交通，带走钥匙并锁车
尽量停在靠车流一侧并让发动机运转
把钥匙留在点火开关上以备紧急情况

explanation.en: When parking by a road: park as far from traffic as possible and close to the curb, set the parking brake, use gear (manual) or Park (automatic), check mirrors and traffic before opening the door, and take your keys and lock the vehicle. See Section 3: Basic Driving.
explanation.zh: 路边停车时：尽量远离车流并靠近路缘，拉手刹，手动挡挂挡或自动挡挂P挡，开门前查看镜子和交通，带走钥匙并锁车。见第3节：基本驾驶。

q.en: You are entering a traffic circle (roundabout). Traffic is already circulating inside. What must you do?
q.zh: 你正进入环岛，岛内已有车辆在环行。你必须怎么做？

en: Stop at the yield line even when the circle is empty and wait one minute
Drive to the left of the island if it is shorter
Enter quickly — entering traffic has priority
Always yield to traffic already in the circle, keep right of the island, and yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk
zh: 即使环岛为空也要在让行线停一分钟
如果更近可以从中心岛左侧走
快速进入——进入车辆优先
始终让行已在环岛内的车辆，保持在中心岛右侧，并让行人行横道上的行人

explanation.en: At a traffic circle you must always yield to traffic already in the circle, reduce speed, keep to the right of the island, and watch for pedestrians in the crosswalk. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 在环岛处必须始终让行已在岛内的车辆，减速，保持在中心岛右侧，并注意人行横道上的行人。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: You missed your exit on an interstate highway. What must you never do?
q.zh: 你在州际公路上错过了出口。绝不能做什么？

en: Never stop and back up on any part of the highway — continue off the ramp and find a way to re-enter
Use the shoulder to reverse to the exit
Continue to the next exit
Make a U-turn across the median
zh: 绝不能在高速公路任何部分停车倒车——应继续驶离匝道再找路返回

explanation.en: If you exit at the wrong place, continue until you are off the exit ramp, then look for a way to re-enter. Never stop and back up on any part of the highway. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 如果走错出口，应继续驶离出口匝道，再寻找重新进入的办法。绝不能在高速公路任何部分停车倒车。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: Your car breaks down on an interstate and you pull onto the shoulder. What does the manual advise?
q.zh: 你的车在州际公路上抛锚，你停到路肩上。手册建议怎么做？

en: Leave the flashers off to save the battery
Walk along the highway to the nearest exit
Turn on your emergency flashers and stay inside your vehicle if you can
Stand behind the car and wave traffic around
zh: 沿高速公路步行到最近的出口
打开危险报警灯，并尽量留在车内
站在车后挥手指挥交通绕行

explanation.en: On an interstate shoulder: turn on emergency flashers to warn other drivers and stay inside your vehicle if you can — standing or walking along an interstate is very dangerous. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 在州际公路路肩：打开危险报警灯警告其他驾驶员，并尽量留在车内——在州际公路旁站立或行走非常危险。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: A police officer is directing traffic and waves you through a red light. A school crossing guard in uniform is also nearby. When may you disobey a traffic control device?
q.zh: 一名警察正在指挥交通并挥手让你通过红灯，附近还有一名穿制服的学校过街护导员。何时可以不服从交通控制装置？

en: Never — devices always override people
Whenever you are in a hurry
Only when a police officer, emergency personnel, or a uniformed school crossing guard directs you to do something different
Whenever traffic is light
zh: 永不——装置永远优先于人
只有当警察、应急人员或穿制服的学校过街护导员指示你采取不同行动时

explanation.en: The only time you do not obey traffic control devices is when a police officer or other emergency personnel, or a school crossing guard in uniform, tells you to do something different. See Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings.
explanation.zh: 唯一可以不服从交通控制装置的情况是警察或其他应急人员、或穿制服的学校过街护导员指示你采取不同行动时。见第4节：标志、信号与路面标线。

source.section: Section 4: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings

q.en: On a dry road in ideal conditions, what minimum following distance does the MVA recommend?
q.zh: 在理想条件下干燥路面上，MVA建议的最小跟车距离是多少？

en: 10 seconds
3 to 4 seconds
1 second
2 seconds

explanation.en: The MVA recommends a minimum following distance of 3 to 4 seconds under ideal driving conditions, measured by counting as the vehicle ahead passes a fixed reference point. See Section 3: Basic Driving.
explanation.zh: MVA建议理想条件下最小跟车距离为3到4秒，用前车经过固定参照物后开始计数的方法测量。见第3节：基本驾驶。

q.en: You are following a delivery van that stops frequently. How should you adjust your following distance?
q.zh: 你跟在一辆经常停车的送货车后面。应如何调整跟车距离？

en: Keep it exactly the same as for any car
Increase it to four or five seconds, and possibly more if needed
Follow closer so you can pass sooner
Reduce it to 1 second so others cannot cut in
zh: 与跟随普通轿车完全一样
增加到四到五秒，需要时还可以更多
跟得更近以便更早超越
减到1秒，防止别人插进来

explanation.en: When following vehicles that stop often, such as buses and delivery vans, increase the distance to four or five seconds, and possibly more if needed. See Section 3: Basic Driving.
explanation.zh: 跟随经常停车的车辆（如公交车、送货车）时，应将距离增加到四到五秒，需要时还可以更多。见第3节：基本驾驶。

q.en: Which of these does NOT affect your vehicle's stopping distance?
q.zh: 以下哪项不会影响你车辆的停车距离？

en: The type and condition of the road
The condition of your tires and brakes
The time it takes you to notice a dangerous situation
The color of your vehicle
zh: 你注意到危险情况所需的时间

explanation.en: Stopping distance depends on how long it takes you to see a dangerous situation, the type and condition of the road, tire tread condition, and brake condition — not on vehicle color. See Section 3: Basic Driving.
explanation.zh: 停车距离取决于你察觉危险所需的时间、道路类型和状况、轮胎花纹状况和刹车状况——与车辆颜色无关。见第3节：基本驾驶。

q.en: Rain is falling and your windshield wipers are running. What does Maryland law require?
q.zh: 正在下雨，你的雨刷在工作。马里兰州法律要求什么？

en: Turn on your headlights whenever you use your windshield wipers in inclement weather
Use hazard lights instead of headlights
Turn on your high beams
Turn off your headlights to reduce glare
zh: 在恶劣天气使用雨刷时打开大灯
用危险报警灯代替大灯

explanation.en: Maryland law requires you to turn on your headlights when using your windshield wipers in inclement weather. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 马里兰州法律要求在恶劣天气使用雨刷时打开大灯。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: On an unlit road at night you are using high beams. A car approaches from the opposite direction. When must you switch to low beams?
q.zh: 夜间在没有路灯的路上你使用远光灯。对面有车驶来。你必须在多远时切换为近光灯？

en: At least 500 feet before reaching it
At least 100 feet before reaching it
Only after it passes you
At least 300 feet before reaching it
zh: 到达其前方至少500英尺时
到达其前方至少100英尺时
到达其前方至少300英尺时

explanation.en: Change to low beams at least 500 feet before reaching vehicles coming toward you, and when following a vehicle that is 300 feet or less in front of you. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 应在距对向车辆至少500英尺时切换为近光灯；跟随前方300英尺以内的车辆时也应使用近光灯。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: You are following another vehicle closely at night. At what distance must you be using low beams instead of high beams?
q.zh: 夜间你正近距离跟随另一辆车。在多远距离内必须使用近光灯而非远光灯？

en: 300 feet or less
50 feet or less
1,000 feet or less
500 feet or less

explanation.en: Change to low beams when following a vehicle that is 300 feet or less in front of you. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 跟随前方300英尺或更近的车辆时，应切换为近光灯。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: Visibility drops until you cannot clearly see a certain distance ahead. Headlights must be on whenever you cannot clearly see at least:
q.zh: 能见度下降，直到你无法看清前方一定距离。看不清至少多远时必须打开大灯？

en: 2,000 feet
500 feet
200 feet
1,000 feet

explanation.en: You must turn on your headlights anytime there is not enough light to clearly see at least 1,000 feet in front of your vehicle. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 每当光线不足以看清车辆前方至少1000英尺时，必须打开大灯。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: In fog, which headlight setting should you use?
q.zh: 在雾中，应使用哪种大灯设置？

en: Hazard lights only
High beams only
Low beams only, plus fog lights if you have them
No lights, to avoid glare
zh: 只用近光灯，如有雾灯也打开

explanation.en: In fog, use low beam headlights only, and fog lights if equipped. High beams make it harder to see in fog. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 在雾中只使用近光灯，如有雾灯则一并打开。远光灯会使雾中更难看清。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: The fog becomes so thick that you cannot drive safely. What should you do?
q.zh: 雾浓到无法安全驾驶。你应该怎么做？

en: Pull completely off the road to a safe location and turn on your emergency flashers
Follow the taillights ahead very closely
Stop in your travel lane and wait
Keep driving slowly in the left lane
zh: 完全驶离道路到安全地点，并打开危险报警灯
在左侧车道慢慢继续开

explanation.en: If fog is so thick you cannot safely drive, pull completely off the road to a safe location and turn on your emergency flashers. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 如果雾浓到无法安全驾驶，应完全驶离道路到安全地点，并打开危险报警灯。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: Your vehicle begins to skid on a wet curve. What is the correct first response?
q.zh: 你的车在湿弯道上开始打滑。正确的第一反应是什么？

en: Brake as hard as possible
Release the accelerator or brake pedal you are using, steer in the direction of the skid, and look where you want to go
Steer opposite to the skid
Accelerate quickly to regain grip
zh: 松开正在使用的油门或刹车踏板，向打滑方向打方向，并看向你想去的方向
向打滑的反方向打方向
快速加速以恢复抓地力

explanation.en: In a skid: release the accelerator or brake pedal, steer in the direction you are skidding, look where you want the vehicle to go, and press the brake only after traction returns. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 打滑时：松开油门或刹车踏板，向打滑方向打方向，看向你想去的方向，待抓地力恢复后再踩刹车。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: Driving fast through standing water, your tires ride up on a sheet of water and you lose contact with the road. This is called hydroplaning. What should you do?
q.zh: 快速驶过积水时，轮胎浮在水面上失去与路面的接触。这叫水滑（hydroplaning）。你应该怎么做？

en: Speed up to push through the water
Turn the wheel sharply toward the shoulder
Take your foot off the gas, do not apply the brakes, keep the vehicle going straight, and slow down until you regain control
Brake firmly at once
zh: 松开油门，不踩刹车，保持车辆直行，减速直到恢复控制

explanation.en: To recover from hydroplaning: take your foot off the gas, do not apply the brakes, keep the vehicle going straight, and slow down until you get control back. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 水滑后恢复控制的方法：松开油门，不踩刹车，保持车辆直行，减速直到恢复控制。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: Which road surfaces freeze first in cold weather and deserve extra caution?
q.zh: 在寒冷天气里，哪些路面最先结冰，需要格外小心？

en: Ramps and bridges
Toll plazas
Straight flat highways
Parking lots

explanation.en: Ramps and bridges freeze before roads. Plowed roads may also refreeze at night or keep icy patches from melted snow. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 匝道和桥梁比道路先结冰。已清雪的道路夜间也可能重新结冰或留有融雪后的冰斑。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: A thin, nearly invisible layer of ice on asphalt, formed by melting and re-freezing, is known as:
q.zh: 沥青路面上由融化和再冻结形成的薄而几乎看不见的冰层被称为：

en: Sheet rain
White frost
Road glaze paint
Black ice

explanation.en: That thin layer of ice on blacktop roads is called black ice. It is caused by ice or snow melting and re-freezing and can cause a crash if you are not aware of it. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 沥青路面上的这种薄冰层称为黑冰。它由冰雪融化后再次冻结形成，如不警觉可能导致事故。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: Before driving in snow or ice, which preparation does the manual require?
q.zh: 在冰雪中驾驶前，手册要求做哪项准备？

en: Remove your mirrors
Turn off your headlights
Remove all ice and snow from your vehicle before driving
Let air out of your tires
zh: 驾驶前清除车辆上所有冰雪

explanation.en: Remove all ice and snow from your vehicle before driving in winter weather, start very slowly, test your brakes gently, and begin slowing long before intersections or turns. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 冬季驾驶前应清除车辆上所有冰雪，起步要非常缓慢，轻试刹车，并在路口或转弯前很早就开始减速。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: Gates are down and red warning lights are flashing at a railroad crossing, but you see no train. What must you do?
q.zh: 铁路道口栏杆已放下、红色警告灯闪烁，但你没看到火车。你必须怎么做？

en: Stop and wait — the road is temporarily closed until the gates go up and the lights stop flashing
Cross only in the oncoming lane
Drive around the gates slowly
Cross quickly before the train arrives
zh: 停车等待——在栏杆升起、警告灯停止闪烁前道路暂时封闭
在火车到来前快速通过

explanation.en: If gates are down or warning lights are flashing, the road is temporarily closed. Stop and wait until the gates go up and the warning lights stop flashing. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 栏杆放下或警告灯闪烁时，道路暂时封闭。应停车等待，直到栏杆升起且警告灯停止闪烁。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: A train has just passed and the gates are rising. Before crossing, what must you check?
q.zh: 一列火车刚通过，栏杆正在升起。通过前你必须检查什么？

en: Wave to the driver behind you
Nothing — one train means the tracks are clear
Check only your mirrors
Look both ways — another train may be coming on another track
zh: 什么都不用——过了一列火车就说明轨道通畅
左右观察——另一条轨道上可能有另一列火车驶来

explanation.en: After a train passes, look both ways before starting over the tracks and make sure the tracks are clear; another train may be coming on another track. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 火车通过后，驶上轨道前应左右观察并确认轨道通畅；另一条轨道上可能有另一列火车驶来。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: Which vehicles must stop before every railroad crossing?
q.zh: 哪些车辆必须在每个铁路道口前停车？

en: Only vehicles over 10 years old
Buses, school buses, and trucks carrying hazardous materials
All passenger cars
Only motorcycles
zh: 公交车、校车和运载危险品的卡车

explanation.en: Buses, school buses, and trucks carrying hazardous materials must stop before every railroad crossing, so be aware of vehicles stopping ahead of you at crossings. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 公交车、校车和运载危险品的卡车必须在每个铁路道口前停车，因此要注意前方车辆在道口停车。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: You enter a work zone where workers are present. Which statement is correct?
q.zh: 你进入一个有工人在场的施工区。下列哪项正确？

en: You may ignore temporary signs
Speeding fines may be much higher in work zones, and even higher if workers are present; flashing blue lights mean speed cameras are active
Orange signs are only suggestions
Speed limits do not apply in work zones
zh: 施工区超速罚款可能高得多，有工人时更高；蓝色闪灯表示测速摄像头正在工作

explanation.en: In work zones, obey posted limits — fines may be much higher, and higher still if workers are present. Flashing amber/yellow lights mean an active work zone with workers present; flashing blue lights mean active speed cameras. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 在施工区应遵守标示限速——罚款可能高得多，有工人时更高。琥珀/黄色闪灯表示有工人的活跃施工区；蓝色闪灯表示测速摄像头正在工作。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: A vehicle displaying a slow-moving vehicle sign on its rear is traveling at what speed?
q.zh: 后部带有慢行车辆标志的车辆，行驶速度是多少？

en: 25 mph or less
15 mph or less
35 mph or less
40 mph or less

explanation.en: The slow-moving vehicle sign warns that the vehicle is going 25 miles per hour or less. Pass such vehicles only when it is safe. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 慢行车辆标志表示该车速度为25英里/小时或更低。只在安全时才超越这类车辆。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: Your eyes keep closing, you cannot stop yawning, and you do not remember the last few miles. These are danger signs of drowsy driving. What is the best action?
q.zh: 你的眼睛不断闭合、打哈欠停不下来，且不记得刚才几英里的路。这些是疲劳驾驶的危险信号。最好的做法是什么？

en: Rest or change drivers — being tired dulls your mind and slows your reactions
Drink an energy drink and speed up
Turn the radio up loud
Open the window and keep driving
zh: 休息或换驾驶员——疲劳会使思维迟钝、反应变慢

explanation.en: If you become tired or sleepy while driving, it is best to rest or change drivers. Sleepiness slows reaction time, decreases awareness, and impairs judgment, much like drugs or alcohol. See Section 6: Dangerous Driving Behaviors.
explanation.zh: 驾驶时感到疲倦或困倦，最好休息或更换驾驶员。困倦会减慢反应、降低警觉并损害判断力，与毒品或酒精类似。见第6节：危险驾驶行为。

q.en: Which of these counts as distracted driving according to the manual?
q.zh: 根据手册，以下哪项属于分心驾驶？

en: Checking your mirrors
Listening to traffic reports with hands on the wheel and eyes on the road is the only example
Using your turn signal
Eating, programming a GPS, dealing with children or pets, or reading — anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off driving
zh: 手握方向盘、眼看道路听交通广播是唯一例子
吃东西、设置GPS、照看孩子或宠物、阅读——任何使眼睛、手或注意力离开驾驶的行为

explanation.en: Distracted driving is taking your eyes, hands, or especially your mind away from driving. Examples include eating and drinking, adjusting the radio, programming a GPS, dealing with children and pets, loose objects, talking or texting on a phone, smoking, makeup, shaving, and reading. See Section 6: Dangerous Driving Behaviors.
explanation.zh: 分心驾驶是指眼睛、手，尤其是注意力离开驾驶。例子包括吃喝、调收音机、设置GPS、照看孩子和宠物、松散物品、用电话通话或发短信、吸烟、化妆、刮胡子和阅读。见第6节：危险驾驶行为。

q.en: By law, who in a motor vehicle in Maryland must wear a safety belt or be buckled in a child safety seat?
q.zh: 按法律，马里兰州机动车内的哪些人必须系安全带或固定在儿童安全座椅中？

en: Only children
Only the driver
The driver and all passengers
Only front-seat passengers

explanation.en: By law, the driver and all passengers of a motor vehicle must wear a safety belt or be buckled in a child safety seat. See Section 10: Other Important Information.
explanation.zh: 按法律，机动车驾驶员和所有乘客都必须系安全带或固定在儿童安全座椅中。见第10节：其他重要信息。

q.en: All children under what age must ride in a child safety seat, unless the child is 4 feet 9 inches or taller?
q.zh: 除非身高达4英尺9英寸或更高，多大以下的儿童必须乘坐儿童安全座椅？

en: Under age 6
Under age 8
Under age 12
Under age 5

explanation.en: All children under age 8 must ride in a child safety seat, unless the child is 4'9" or taller. Children under age 2 must ride rear-facing until they reach the manufacturer's height or weight limit. See Section 10: Other Important Information.
explanation.zh: 8岁以下儿童必须乘坐儿童安全座椅，除非身高达到4英尺9英寸或更高。2岁以下儿童必须使用后向式座椅，直到达到制造商规定的身高或体重上限。见第10节：其他重要信息。

q.en: Children under what age must ride in a rear-facing child safety seat until reaching the manufacturer's height or weight limit?
q.zh: 多大以下的儿童必须使用后向式儿童安全座椅，直到达到制造商规定的身高或体重上限？

en: Under age 4
Under age 1
Under age 2
Under age 8

explanation.en: Children younger than 2 must ride in a rear-facing child safety seat that meets federal guidelines until they reach the height or weight specified by the manufacturer. See Section 10: Other Important Information.
explanation.zh: 2岁以下儿童必须使用符合联邦标准的后向式儿童安全座椅，直到达到制造商规定的身高或体重。见第10节：其他重要信息。

q.en: Where should children under age 13 ride, according to the manual?
q.zh: 根据手册，13岁以下儿童应坐在哪里？

en: On an adult's lap
In the front seat with an air bag
Buckled up in a rear seat, in a child safety seat or with a seat belt
Standing behind the front seats
zh: 后排座位，固定在儿童安全座椅中或系安全带

explanation.en: Children under age 13 should ride buckled up in a rear seat in a child safety seat or with a seat belt, and a child in a rear-facing seat should never ride in the front seat of a vehicle with a passenger air bag. See Section 10: Other Important Information.
explanation.zh: 13岁以下儿童应系好安全带坐在后排，固定在儿童安全座椅中或系安全带；使用后向式座椅的儿童绝不能坐在有乘客气囊的前排。见第10节：其他重要信息。

q.en: When your vehicle's ABS engages during hard braking, what may you feel and hear?
q.zh: 紧急刹车时车辆ABS启动，你可能会感觉和听到什么？

en: The horn sounds automatically
The engine shuts off
The steering wheel locks completely
A rumble from the brakes and the brake pedal vibrating under your foot
zh: 刹车发出隆隆声，刹车踏板在脚下振动

explanation.en: When ABS engages you may hear a rumble from the brakes and the brake pedal will vibrate under your foot. ABS pumps the brakes faster than a driver can so the wheels do not lock and steering control is kept. See Section 10: Other Important Information.
explanation.zh: ABS启动时，你可能听到刹车隆隆声并感到刹车踏板在脚下振动。ABS以比人更快的速度点刹，使车轮不锁死并保持转向控制。见第10节：其他重要信息。

q.en: You are in a crash in which someone, including a pedestrian or bicyclist, is injured. What must you do?
q.zh: 你发生了一起有人受伤的事故，包括行人或骑行者受伤。你必须怎么做？

en: Remain at the scene, call 911 immediately, and do not move the vehicles
Leave and report it later from home
Exchange phone numbers and drive away
Move the vehicles first, then decide whether to call
zh: 留在现场，立即拨打911，且不要移动车辆
离开现场，回家后再报告
交换电话号码后驾车离开
先移动车辆，再决定是否报警

explanation.en: In an injury crash you must remain at the scene, call 911 immediately to report the people involved, the injuries, and the location, and not move the vehicles. See Section 8: Crashes and Traffic Stops.
explanation.zh: 在有人受伤的事故中，必须留在现场，立即拨打911报告涉及人数、伤情和地点，且不要移动车辆。见第8节：事故与交通拦截。

q.en: In a crash with no injuries where your vehicle can still move, what should you do with the vehicle?
q.zh: 在无人受伤且车辆仍能移动的事故中，你应如何处理车辆？

en: Leave it in the travel lane with flashers on
Drive it home before exchanging information
Move it off the road as close as possible to where the crash occurred, then exchange information
Push it into the nearest intersection
zh: 让它留在行车道上并打开报警灯
把它移出道路，尽量靠近事故发生地点，然后交换信息

explanation.en: If there are no injuries and your vehicle can move, move it off the road as close as possible to the crash location to keep everyone safe and prevent backups, then exchange information with the other driver. See Section 8: Crashes and Traffic Stops.
explanation.zh: 如果无人受伤且车辆能移动，应把它移出道路并尽量靠近事故地点，以保安全并防堵车，然后与对方驾驶员交换信息。见第8节：事故与交通拦截。

q.en: You strike an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find its owner. What are you required to do?
q.zh: 你撞到一辆无人看管的停放车辆，且找不到车主。你必须怎么做？

en: Wait exactly five minutes, then leave
Drive away — no one saw it
Leave only your first name
Leave a note where the owner can easily find it, explaining what happened and giving your contact information
zh: 在车主容易找到的地方留一张字条，说明发生的事情并留下你的联系方式

explanation.en: If you cannot find the owner of an unattended vehicle or property you struck, leave a note where they can easily find it, describing what happened and giving your contact information. See Section 8: Crashes and Traffic Stops.
explanation.zh: 如果你找不到被撞的无人车辆或财物的主人，应在对方容易找到的地方留一张字条，说明经过并留下联系方式。见第8节：事故与交通拦截。

q.en: During a traffic stop, where should your hands be and what should you avoid doing?
q.zh: 在交通拦截期间，你的手应放在哪里，应避免做什么？

en: Reach into the glove box quickly before the officer arrives
Get out and walk toward the officer
Hide your hands so the officer is not nervous
Keep your hands in plain view — on the steering wheel is best — stay in the vehicle with your seat belt fastened, and do not argue about a citation at the roadside
zh: 在警官到达前快速伸手去手套箱
把手藏起来免得警官紧张
让双手清楚可见——放在方向盘上最好——留在车内系好安全带，不要在路边就罚单争辩

explanation.en: At a traffic stop: pull off as far from traffic as possible, turn on flashers, turn off the engine and radio, roll down your window, stay in the vehicle with your seat belt fastened, keep hands in plain view on the steering wheel, and save any argument about a citation for court. See Section 8: Crashes and Traffic Stops.
explanation.zh: 交通拦截时：将车停到尽量远离车流处，打开报警灯，关闭发动机和收音机，摇下车窗，留在车内系好安全带，双手放在方向盘上清楚可见，对罚单的异议留到法庭提出。见第8节：事故与交通拦截。

q.en: There is no traffic signal, and a pedestrian is in an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection. What must you do?
q.zh: 没有交通信号灯，一名行人正在路口无标线的人行横道上。你必须怎么做？

en: Honk so the pedestrian hurries
Stop for the pedestrian — drivers must stop for pedestrians in a marked or unmarked crosswalk when there is no signal
Pass behind the pedestrian quickly
Continue — unmarked crosswalks do not count
zh: 为行人停车——无信号时，驾驶员必须为在有标线或无标线人行横道上的行人停车
继续——无标线人行横道不算数

explanation.en: When there is no traffic signal, you must stop for pedestrians in a marked or unmarked crosswalk. Most intersections have a crosswalk even if it is not marked. See Section 7: Sharing the Road.
explanation.zh: 没有交通信号时，必须为在有标线或无标线人行横道上的行人停车。大多数路口即使没有标线也有人行横道。见第7节：共享道路。

q.en: A car ahead of you has stopped at a crosswalk. May you pass it?
q.zh: 你前方的一辆车在人行横道前停了下来。你可以超越它吗？

en: Yes, on the shoulder
No — you may not pass any vehicle that is stopped at a crosswalk
Yes, on the left if clear
Yes, if you honk first
zh: 不可以——不得超越任何在人行横道前停车的车辆

explanation.en: You may not pass any vehicle that is stopped at a crosswalk — a pedestrian you cannot see may be crossing. See Section 7: Sharing the Road.
explanation.zh: 不得超越任何在人行横道前停车的车辆——可能有你看不到的行人正在过街。见第7节：共享道路。

q.en: You hear a siren and see flashing lights approaching behind you. What must you do immediately?
q.zh: 你听到警笛声并看到闪光灯从后方接近。你必须立即怎么做？

en: Stop in the middle of the intersection
Follow it closely to get through traffic
Speed up to stay ahead of it
Move as close as possible to the edge of the road, stay out of intersections, and remain stopped until the emergency vehicle passes
zh: 尽量靠道路边缘行驶，避开路口，并保持停车直到应急车辆通过

explanation.en: Emergency vehicles using sirens and flashing lights have the right-of-way. Move as close as possible to the edge of the road, stay out of intersections, and remain stopped until the vehicle has passed. See Section 7: Sharing the Road.
explanation.zh: 使用警笛和闪光灯的应急车辆拥有路权。应尽量靠道路边缘，避开路口，并保持停车直到该车通过。见第7节：共享道路。

q.en: You are traveling in the same direction as an ambulance using its lights and siren. When may you pass it?
q.zh: 你与一辆使用灯光和警笛的救护车同向行驶。何时可以超越它？

en: On its right side only
After 30 seconds of following
Whenever your lane is clear
Only if it stops, or a police officer tells you to pass it
zh: 只有当它停下，或警察让你超越时

explanation.en: If you are going the same direction as an emergency vehicle using its signals, you may not pass it unless it stops or a police officer tells you to pass. See Section 7: Sharing the Road.
explanation.zh: 与使用信号的应急车辆同向时，不得超越它，除非它停下或警察让你超越。见第7节：共享道路。

q.en: You approach a tow truck stopped on the shoulder with its lights flashing, and the lane next to it is open. Under Maryland's Move Over law, what must you do?
q.zh: 你接近一辆停在路肩、闪光灯亮着的拖车，旁边车道空着。根据马里兰州“让行法”（Move Over），你必须怎么做？

en: Stop completely behind it
Pass it at full speed in the adjacent lane
Honk and continue
Move to a lane that is not immediately next to the stopped vehicle; if you cannot move over safely, slow down to a safe speed
zh: 变道到不与停靠车辆紧邻的车道；如果无法安全变道，则减速到安全速度

explanation.en: When approaching any vehicle stopped, standing, or parked with its lights flashing, you must move over if you can; if it is not safe or possible, slow down to a safe speed considering weather, road conditions, traffic, and pedestrians. See Section 8: Crashes and Traffic Stops.
explanation.zh: 接近任何停车、停放且闪光灯亮着的车辆时，必须在可能时变道让开；如果不安全或无法做到，则应考虑天气、路况、交通和行人，减速到安全速度。见第8节：事故与交通拦截。

q.en: A driver violates the Move Over law and the violation causes a crash. What penalty does the manual state?
q.zh: 一名驾驶员违反“让行法”并导致了一起事故。手册规定的处罚是什么？

en: A $150 fine and three points
A $110 fine and one point
A $750 fine and three points
A warning only

explanation.en: Move Over penalties: a $110 fine and one point for a basic violation; a $150 fine and three points if the violation causes a crash; a $750 fine and three points if there is a death or serious injury. See Section 8: Crashes and Traffic Stops.
explanation.zh: “让行法”处罚：一般违法罚款110美元和1分；导致事故的罚款150美元和3分；导致死亡或重伤的罚款750美元和3分。见第8节：事故与交通拦截。

q.en: A Move Over violation results in a death or serious injury. What is the stated penalty?
q.zh: 一起“让行法”违法导致了死亡或重伤。规定的处罚是什么？

en: A $110 fine and one point
A $150 fine and three points
A $750 fine and three points
No fine, only points

explanation.en: If a Move Over violation results in a death or serious injury, the penalty is a $750 fine and three points on the license. See Section 8: Crashes and Traffic Stops.
explanation.zh: 如果“让行法”违法导致死亡或重伤，处罚是罚款750美元并在驾照上记3分。见第8节：事故与交通拦截。

q.en: A school bus ahead of you stops and turns on its flashing red lights. You are behind it. Where must you stop?
q.zh: 你前方的一辆校车停下并打开红色闪光灯。你在它后面。你必须在哪里停车？

en: Right at its bumper
At least 5 feet behind it
You do not need to stop if no children are visible
At least 20 feet from the back of the school bus
zh: 如果看不到儿童就不用停
距校车后部至少20英尺处

explanation.en: Stop at least 20 feet from the back of the school bus if you are behind it, or at least 20 feet from the front if you are in front of it, and do not move again until the bus moves or turns off its flashing red lights. See Section 7: Sharing the Road.
explanation.zh: 在校车后面时，应距其后部至少20英尺停车；在校车前方时，应距其前部至少20英尺停车，并且在校车移动或关闭红色闪光灯前不得再行驶。见第7节：共享道路。

q.en: You approach a stopped school bus with flashing red lights from the opposite direction on a multi-lane road divided by a physical barrier, and the bus is on the other side of the barrier. What must you do?
q.zh: 你从对面接近一辆打开红色闪光灯的停靠校车，这是一条由物理屏障分隔的多车道道路，校车在屏障另一侧。你必须怎么做？

en: Stop at least 20 feet from the bus
Slow to 5 mph and pass
Stop only if children are crossing toward you
You do not need to stop, because the bus is on the other side of a physical barrier
zh: 减速到5英里/小时并通过
只有儿童朝你这边过街时才停
不需要停车，因为校车在物理屏障的另一侧

explanation.en: If you are on a multiple-lane road divided by a physical barrier, do not stop if the bus is on the other side of the barrier. In other cases you must stop at least 20 feet from the bus. See Section 7: Sharing the Road.
explanation.zh: 如果是在由物理屏障分隔的多车道道路上，校车在屏障另一侧时不需要停车。其他情况下必须距校车至少20英尺停车。见第7节：共享道路。

q.en: A large truck ahead signals right and swings wide to the left before turning. What is the risk if you try to pass it on the right?
q.zh: 前方一辆大卡车打右转灯，先向左大幅摆动再转弯。如果你试图从右侧超越它，有什么风险？

en: You could be caught between the turning truck and the curb; wait to see whether the truck is turning before passing
You will save time safely
None — the truck is leaving your lane
The truck driver can always see you on the right
zh: 你可能被夹在转弯的卡车和路缘之间；应先确认卡车是否在转弯再决定是否超越
没有风险——卡车正在离开你的车道
卡车司机总能看到右侧的你

explanation.en: Trucks make wide turns and often move left before a right turn. Passing a truck on the right can be risky — never cut in along its right side as it begins to turn. See Section 7: Sharing the Road.
explanation.zh: 卡车转弯半径大，右转前常先向左摆动。从右侧超越卡车有风险——当它开始转弯时，绝不能从其右侧切入。见第7节：共享道路。

q.en: You have just passed a large truck. When is it safe to move back in front of it?
q.zh: 你刚超越一辆大卡车。何时可以安全地回到它前面？

en: When the truck honks
As soon as you are one car-length ahead
After signaling for one second
Only when you can see both of the truck's headlights in your rear-view mirror — never cut in front of a truck, which needs almost twice the time and room of a car to stop
zh: 只要领先一个车身就可以
只有在后视镜中能看到卡车的两个大灯后——绝不能切到卡车前面，卡车停车所需的时间和距离几乎是轿车的两倍

explanation.en: Do not move in front of a truck or bus too soon after passing: wait until you can see both of its headlights in your rear-view mirror, and do not slow down. See Section 7: Sharing the Road.
explanation.zh: 超越卡车或公交车后不要太早回到其前方：等到在后视镜中能看到它的两个大灯后再并入，且不要减速。见第7节：共享道路。

q.en: Truck blind spots are called no-zones. If you cannot see the truck driver's face in the truck's side-view mirror:
q.zh: 卡车的盲区被称为“no-zones”（盲区）。如果你在卡车的侧视镜中看不到卡车司机的脸：

en: The driver is looking the other way on purpose
You are in the safest position
The driver cannot see you
The driver can still see you

explanation.en: If you cannot see the truck driver's face in their side-view mirror, they cannot see you. Trucks and buses have four large blind spots — side, rear, front, and backing no-zones. See Section 7: Sharing the Road.
explanation.zh: 如果你在侧视镜中看不到卡车司机的脸，对方也看不到你。卡车和公交车有四个大盲区——侧面、后方、前方和倒车盲区。见第7节：共享道路。

q.en: You are turning left and a motorcycle is approaching from the opposite direction. What does the manual require?
q.zh: 你正在左转，一辆摩托车从对面驶来。手册要求什么？

en: Motorcycles always go last
Turn quickly — motorcycles must yield to cars
Yield the right-of-way to the oncoming motorcycle; failing to yield can bring a citation with significant penalties and cause serious injury
Turn only if you honk first
zh: 快速转弯——摩托车必须让轿车
让行对向摩托车；不让行可能被开罚单并受重罚，还可能造成严重伤害

explanation.en: Yield right-of-way to an oncoming motorcycle when turning left. Drivers are at fault in over half of car crashes with motorcycles. See Section 7: Sharing the Road.
explanation.zh: 左转时应让行对向摩托车。在汽车与摩托车的事故中，超过一半是汽车驾驶员的责任。见第7节：共享道路。

q.en: How much following distance should you leave behind a motorcycle, and why might the motorcycle slow without its brake light appearing?
q.zh: 你应在摩托车后留多少跟车距离？为什么摩托车可能在刹车灯不亮的情况下减速？

en: Half a car length; brake lights are optional
At least a 3 to 4-second following distance; motorcyclists may reduce speed for road hazards in ways that do not trigger the brake light
10 seconds; motorcycles never slow down
1 second; brake lights always appear
zh: 半个车身；刹车灯是可选的
至少3到4秒跟车距离；骑行者可能因路面危险以不触发刹车灯的方式减速

explanation.en: Leave at least a 3 to 4-second following distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcyclists may slow for hazards like gravel or wet roads in ways that do not cause their brake lights to come on. See Section 7: Sharing the Road.
explanation.zh: 应在摩托车后留至少3到4秒跟车距离。骑行者可能因碎石、湿路等危险以不点亮刹车灯的方式减速。见第7节：共享道路。

q.en: When passing a bicyclist in the same lane, how much space must you leave between your vehicle and the bicycle?
q.zh: 在同一车道超越骑行者时，你的车辆与自行车之间必须留多少空间？

en: At least 2 feet
At least 3 feet
At least 1 foot
No minimum, as long as you do not touch the bicycle
zh: 没有最低要求，只要不碰到自行车

explanation.en: Leave at least 3 feet between your vehicle and the bicycle when passing — in a bike lane, on the shoulder, or in the same lane — and see the bicycle in your rear-view mirror before returning to your lane. See Section 7: Sharing the Road.
explanation.zh: 超车时你的车辆与自行车之间至少留3英尺——无论是在自行车道、路肩还是同一车道——并在后视镜中看到自行车后再返回车道。见第7节：共享道路。

q.en: A bicyclist is riding in the center of a narrow travel lane, well below the speed of traffic, because the lane is too narrow for a car to pass safely within it. Is this allowed in Maryland?
q.zh: 一名骑行者在一狭窄车道中央行驶，速度远低于车流，因为该车道太窄，汽车无法在车道内安全超越。在马里兰州这允许吗？

en: Only if the bicyclist is over 18
Only on weekends
Yes — a bicyclist may use the full lane, even well below traffic speed, when the lane is too narrow for a motor vehicle to pass safely in the lane
No — bicyclists must always hug the curb
zh: 只有骑行者年满18岁才行
允许——当车道太窄、机动车无法在车道内安全超越时，骑行者可以使用整条车道，即使速度远低于车流
不允许——骑行者必须始终贴路缘

explanation.en: In Maryland a bicyclist may use the full lane even while traveling significantly below the speed of traffic if the lane is too narrow for a motor vehicle to safely pass the bicycle within the lane. See Section 7: Sharing the Road.
explanation.zh: 在马里兰州，如果车道太窄、机动车无法在车道内安全超越自行车，骑行者可以使用整条车道，即使速度明显低于车流。见第7节：共享道路。

q.en: You approach a bicyclist from behind on a quiet road. Why should you avoid honking your horn?
q.zh: 在一条安静的路上你从后方接近一名骑行者。为什么应避免鸣笛？

en: It is only a problem at night
Horns are banned everywhere in Maryland
Honking uses too much battery
Bicyclists can usually hear an approaching vehicle, and a loud noise can startle them and cause a crash
zh: 马里兰州各地都禁止鸣笛
骑行者通常能听到接近的车辆，响亮的声响可能惊吓他们并导致事故

explanation.en: As you approach a bicyclist, slow down and do not honk your horn. Bicyclists can usually hear an approaching vehicle, and loud noises can startle them, causing a crash. See Section 7: Sharing the Road.
explanation.zh: 接近骑行者时应减速且不要鸣笛。骑行者通常能听到接近的车辆，巨响可能惊吓他们并导致事故。见第7节：共享道路。

q.en: Mopeds and motor scooters may be ridden on roads with a posted maximum speed limit of:
q.zh: 轻便摩托车和踏板车可以在最高限速为多少的道路上行驶？

en: 25 mph or less
35 mph or less
50 mph or less
Any speed limit

explanation.en: Mopeds and scooters may be ridden on any road with a posted maximum speed limit of 50 miles per hour or less, on the road or on the shoulder, side-by-side or alone. See Section 7: Sharing the Road.
explanation.zh: 轻便摩托车和踏板车可以在最高限速50英里/小时或更低的任何道路上行驶，可在路面或路肩上，可并排或单独行驶。见第7节：共享道路。

q.en: You are driving in a funeral procession with your headlights and hazard flashers on. Another driver facing a green signal reaches the procession's path. What must that driver do?
q.zh: 你正在送葬车队中行驶，开着大灯和危险报警灯。另一名驾驶员面对绿灯来到车队路径上。该驾驶员必须怎么做？

en: Yield the right-of-way to the procession until all its vehicles have passed, unless they can proceed safely without crossing the procession's path
Proceed — green always wins
Pass the procession on the shoulder
Honk until the procession stops
zh: 让行车队，直到车队所有车辆都通过，除非能在不穿越车队路径的情况下安全通过

explanation.en: Even with a green signal, other vehicles must yield the right-of-way to vehicles in a funeral procession until all of them have passed, unless they can safely proceed without crossing the procession's path. See Section 5: Driving Situations and Conditions.
explanation.zh: 即使面对绿灯，其他车辆也必须让行送葬车队，直到车队全部通过，除非能在不穿越车队路径的情况下安全通过。见第5节：驾驶情形与条件。

q.en: In Maryland, a driver is considered to be driving under the influence of alcohol at a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
q.zh: 在马里兰州，血液酒精浓度（BAC）达到多少即被视为酒后驾驶？

en: Any detectable amount, for all drivers
0.08 or higher
0.05 or higher
0.10 or higher
zh: 对所有驾驶员来说只要检测到即可

explanation.en: Maryland considers drivers to be driving under the influence of alcohol when their BAC is .08 or higher. Any amount of alcohol can still impair driving and bring criminal charges at a lower BAC. See Section 6: Dangerous Driving Behaviors.
explanation.zh: 当驾驶员的BAC达到0.08或更高时，马里兰州视为酒后驾驶。任何量的酒精都可能影响驾驶，BAC更低时也可能面临刑事指控。见第6节：危险驾驶行为。

q.en: A driver under 21 is stopped and has been drinking, though his BAC is low. Under the manual, what can happen?
q.zh: 一名21岁以下驾驶员被拦下且饮过酒，尽管BAC较低。根据手册，可能发生什么？

en: Drinking any alcohol is illegal under 21; his license will be suspended or revoked and he can be charged with violating the alcohol restriction on his license
His parents are fined instead
Nothing, if the BAC is under 0.08
Only a verbal warning
zh: 21岁以下饮酒本身违法；他的驾照将被暂停或吊销，并可能因违反驾照上的酒精限制而被指控

explanation.en: If you are not yet 21, it is against the law to drink any alcohol. If stopped after drinking, your license will be suspended or revoked and you could be charged with violating the alcohol restriction on your license. See Section 6: Dangerous Driving Behaviors.
explanation.zh: 未满21岁饮用任何酒精都违法。如果饮酒后被拦下，驾照将被暂停或吊销，并可能因违反驾照上的酒精限制而被指控。见第6节：危险驾驶行为。

q.en: By driving in Maryland, what have you agreed to under the implied consent law?
q.zh: 根据默示同意法（implied consent），在马里兰州驾驶即表示你同意了什么？

en: To install a breathalyzer voluntarily
To take a drug or alcohol test if a law enforcement officer requests one, because driving on a road or public-use private property counts as consent
To allow vehicle searches at any time
To surrender your license on demand without a hearing
zh: 如果执法人员要求，则接受毒品或酒精检测，因为在道路或公众使用的私人财产上驾驶即构成同意
一经要求且无听证即交出驾照

explanation.en: In Maryland, if you drive or attempt to drive on a road or private property used by the public, you consent to take a drug or alcohol test if a law enforcement officer asks you to. See Section 9: Other Restrictions, Violations and Penalties.
explanation.zh: 在马里兰州，如果你在道路或公众使用的私人财产上驾驶或试图驾驶，即表示同意在执法人员要求时接受毒品或酒精检测。见第9节：其他限制、违法与处罚。

source.section: Section 9: Other Restrictions, Violations and Penalties

q.en: An officer submits a certified statement that a driver refused a requested alcohol test. What will the MVA do?
q.zh: 一名警官提交了经认证的声明，称某驾驶员拒绝了要求的酒精检测。MVA会怎么做？

en: The test is rescheduled in 30 days
Nothing — refusal is a protected right with no consequence
The driver receives one point only
The MVA will suspend the driver's license
zh: 什么都不做——拒绝是受保护的权利，无后果
MVA将暂停该驾驶员的驾照

explanation.en: If a police officer submits a certified statement that you refused a test, the MVA will suspend your license. The license is also suspended if your BAC is .08 or higher or you are impaired with drugs in your system. See Section 9: Other Restrictions, Violations and Penalties.
explanation.zh: 如果警官提交经认证的拒绝检测声明，MVA将暂停你的驾照。如果BAC达到0.08或更高，或体内有毒品影响驾驶，驾照也会被暂停。见第9节：其他限制、违法与处罚。

source.section: Section 9: Other Restrictions, Violations and Penalties

q.en: Which statement about judging your own BAC is correct?
q.zh: 关于判断自己的BAC，下列哪项正确？

en: BAC depends only on the type of drink
You cannot tell your BAC by the number of drinks alone — weight, body fat, food, tiredness, mood, and medications all affect how alcohol affects you
Coffee brings BAC down quickly
Two drinks always equals 0.08 for everyone
zh: 不能仅凭杯数判断BAC——体重、体脂、进食、疲劳、情绪和药物都会影响酒精对你的作用
两杯酒对每个人都等于0.08

explanation.en: It is very difficult to know your own BAC or how alcohol is affecting you. You cannot tell by the number of drinks, because weight, body fat, how long ago and how much you ate, tiredness, mood, and medications all make a difference. See Section 6: Dangerous Driving Behaviors.
explanation.zh: 很难知道自己的BAC或酒精对自己的影响。不能仅凭杯数判断，因为体重、体脂、进食时间和量、疲劳、情绪和药物都会产生影响。见第6节：危险驾驶行为。

q.en: After just one drink, which abilities may already be affected?
q.zh: 只喝了一杯酒后，哪些能力可能已经受到影响？

en: Vision, ability to perform simple movements, and reaction time
None — one drink has no effect
Only your hearing
Only your sense of smell
zh: 视力、做简单动作的能力和反应时间
没有——一杯酒没有任何影响

explanation.en: Your vision, ability to perform simple movements, and reaction time may be affected with just one drink, increasing the risk of a crash. See Section 6: Dangerous Driving Behaviors.
explanation.zh: 只喝一杯酒，视力、做简单动作的能力和反应时间就可能受到影响，从而增加事故风险。见第6节：危险驾驶行为。

q.en: An unopened-looking six-pack in the back seat has one can open and one missing. Under Maryland's open container rule:
q.zh: 后座上有一提看似未开封的六罐装啤酒，其中一罐已打开、一罐缺失。根据马里兰州开封容器规定：

en: A six-pack with open, empty, or missing bottles or cans can be considered an open container, and driving with an open container in the passenger area is illegal
It is legal if kept behind the rear seat
It is legal because most cans are sealed
It counts only if the driver drank from it
zh: 一提中有打开、空置或缺失的瓶/罐可被视为开封容器，在乘客区携带开封容器驾驶违法
合法，因为大多数罐是密封的

explanation.en: It is against the law to drive with an open container of alcohol in the passenger area, and a six-pack with open, empty, or missing bottles or cans can be considered an open container. See Section 6: Dangerous Driving Behaviors.
explanation.zh: 在乘客区携带开封的酒精容器驾驶违法；一提中有打开、空置或缺失瓶/罐的，可被视为开封容器。见第6节：危险驾驶行为。

q.en: For the open container law, the 'passenger area' of a vehicle includes:
q.zh: 就开封容器法而言，车辆的“乘客区”包括：

en: Only the front seats
The driver and passenger seats and any place the driver or passengers can easily reach from where they are sitting
Any attached trailer
Only the trunk
zh: 驾驶员和乘客座位，以及驾驶员或乘客坐在座位上容易够到的任何地方

explanation.en: The passenger area includes the driver and passenger seats and any place the driver or passengers can easily reach from where they are sitting. See Section 6: Dangerous Driving Behaviors.
explanation.zh: 乘客区包括驾驶员和乘客座位，以及驾驶员或乘客坐在座位上容易够到的任何地方。见第6节：危险驾驶行为。

q.en: A driver is convicted of a drunk or drugged driving offense while a child was in the vehicle. What extra consequence may apply?
q.zh: 一名驾驶员在车内有儿童时因酒驾或毒驾被定罪。可能适用什么额外后果？

en: The license is automatically upgraded
The judge can double the fine and jail time
No extra consequence
The child receives the points
zh: 法官可以将罚款和监禁时间加倍

explanation.en: If you are convicted of a drunk or drugged driving offense with a child in your vehicle, the judge can double your fine and jail time. See Section 6: Dangerous Driving Behaviors.
explanation.zh: 如果你在车内有儿童时因酒驾或毒驾被定罪，法官可以将你的罚款和监禁时间加倍。见第6节：危险驾驶行为。

q.en: A prescription medication's label warns not to drive while taking it. The driver takes it, is impaired, and drives anyway. What does the manual say?
q.zh: 一种处方药标签警告服药期间不要驾驶。驾驶员服药后受影响仍开车。手册怎么说？

en: Prescription drugs can never lead to charges
The warning is advice only with no legal effect
Only illegal drugs matter
The driver could be charged with a criminal offense for driving after taking a medication that warns against driving when it impairs safe driving
zh: 处方药永不会导致指控
该警告只是建议，无法律效力
如果驾驶员服用了警告不要驾驶的药物且影响安全驾驶，可能被指控刑事罪行

explanation.en: Illegal drugs, some prescription medications, and chemical inhalants can severely affect driving. If you drive after taking a medication that tells you not to and it impairs your ability to drive safely, you could be charged with a criminal offense. See Section 6: Dangerous Driving Behaviors.
explanation.zh: 非法毒品、某些处方药和化学吸入剂会严重影响驾驶。如果你服用了标明不要驾驶的药物后仍开车且影响安全驾驶，可能被指控刑事罪行。见第6节：危险驾驶行为。

q.en: Which of these is a way controlled dangerous substances can affect a driver?
q.zh: 以下哪项是受控危险物质影响驾驶员的方式？

en: They only affect vision
They improve concentration
They can affect alertness, concentration, coordination, and reaction time, and make it hard to judge distances and react to signals and sounds
They have no effect if legally prescribed, in all cases
zh: 它们会影响警觉性、注意力、协调性和反应时间，并使人难以判断距离和对信号和声音作出反应
只要合法处方就永远没有影响

explanation.en: Controlled dangerous substances can affect alertness, concentration, coordination, and reaction time, and all drugs can make it hard to judge distances and react to signals and sounds on the road. See Section 6: Dangerous Driving Behaviors.
explanation.zh: 受控危险物质会影响警觉性、注意力、协调性和反应时间，所有药物都可能使人难以判断距离并对道路上的信号和声音作出反应。见第6节：危险驾驶行为。

q.en: A person caught drinking and driving in Maryland will have to install what device, according to the manual?
q.zh: 根据手册，在马里兰州因酒后驾驶被抓的人必须安装什么装置？

en: A dash camera
A speed limiter set to 25 mph
An ignition interlock — a breathalyzer car lock that prevents starting the vehicle if alcohol is detected
A GPS tracker for one year
zh: 限速25英里/小时的限速器
点火联锁装置——一种酒精检测汽车锁，检测到酒精时阻止车辆启动

explanation.en: A driver caught drinking and driving must install a breathalyzer car lock (ignition interlock) that prevents the vehicle from starting if alcohol is detected. See Section 9: Other Restrictions, Violations and Penalties.
explanation.zh: 因酒后驾驶被抓的驾驶员必须安装酒精检测汽车锁（点火联锁装置），检测到酒精时阻止车辆启动。见第9节：其他限制、违法与处罚。

source.section: Section 9: Other Restrictions, Violations and Penalties

q.en: Lying about your age to buy alcohol can lead to what licensing consequence, besides other penalties?
q.zh: 谎报年龄购买酒精，除其他处罚外，还可能导致什么驾照后果？

en: A free license renewal
Extra practice hours
Nothing beyond a fine in all cases
Your driver's license may be suspended

explanation.en: It is against the law to lie about your age to purchase, possess, or acquire alcohol, and in addition to other penalties your driver's license may be suspended. See Section 9: Other Restrictions, Violations and Penalties.
explanation.zh: 谎报年龄以购买、持有或获取酒精违法，除其他处罚外，你的驾照还可能被暂停。见第9节：其他限制、违法与处罚。

source.section: Section 9: Other Restrictions, Violations and Penalties

q.en: It is illegal to use a hand-held cell phone, including texting, while driving in Maryland. For drivers under 18, the rule is stricter. What is it?
q.zh: 在马里兰州驾驶时使用手持手机（包括发短信）违法。对18岁以下驾驶员，规则更严。是怎样的？

en: They may not use a cell phone while driving at all, even hands-free — the only exception is a 911 emergency call
They may text at red lights
They may use a phone only on highways
They may use hands-free freely
zh: 他们在驾驶时完全不能使用手机，即使是免提也不行——唯一例外是拨打911紧急电话
他们可以在红灯时发短信
他们只能在高速公路上使用手机
他们可以自由使用免提

explanation.en: Drivers under 18 may not use a cell phone while driving, even hands-free; the only exception is a 911 emergency call. Adults may not use a hand-held phone, including texting, while driving. See Section 6: Dangerous Driving Behaviors.
explanation.zh: 18岁以下驾驶员在驾驶时不能使用手机，即使免提也不行；唯一例外是拨打911紧急电话。成年人驾驶时不能使用手持手机，包括发短信。见第6节：危险驾驶行为。

q.en: Which set of behaviors are all examples of aggressive driving given in the manual?
q.zh: 以下哪组行为都是手册列出的攻击性驾驶例子？

en: Speeding, tailgating, ignoring traffic signals, unsafe lane changes, not yielding the right-of-way, and unsafe or illegal passing
